correctness.rationale: The Clifford anticommutation equations give the SLD metric \(J_\theta=(I-\theta\theta^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\). The displayed biased simplex has positive probabilities, mean \(\theta\), and covariance \((1-\|\theta\|^2)I/d\). Transporting it by the score ellipsoid maps every support point to the effect-positivity boundary, so each \(M_i=a_iI+\gamma(b_i)\) is positive and the effects sum to identity. Their local probabilities are \(p_i\), score vectors are \(\ell_i\), and their covariance gives exactly \(F_\theta=J_\theta/d\). For any finite classical outcome model, \(\sum_i p_is_i=0\), so \(m\) positive-probability scores span dimension at most \(m-1\); full-rank \(d\)-dimensional Fisher information therefore requires \(m\ge d+1\). The construction attains equality.

final_claim: For every interior point of a full \(d\)-parameter spin-factor ball with \(d\ge4\), the isotropic SLD-optimal Fisher matrix \(J_\theta/d\) is attained by an explicit \(d+1\)-outcome POVM, and \(d+1\) is the minimum possible number of positive-probability outcomes.
limitations: Only full affine spin-factor balls at interior points and \(d\ge4\) are claimed; no boundary, curved-submodel or parameter-independent global optimality statement is made.
